items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: And they were great players working for — You know at one point Billy Butterfield was getting his 802 card, so was Conrad Gozzo and I. And Billy came in and played third trumpet while he was getting his 802 card.

ctx.x: But what kind of music were you playing?

Well we played just songs. East of the Sun/West of the Moon or something. You know, whatever songs of the day. And Billy and I used to always argue. I liked Louis, he liked Bix. I liked Louis and Bunny of course, but his boy was Bix. And we traded records back and forth, and it took me a while to really appreciate Bix Beiderbecke. Later, yes. But at that time, you know Louis was so straight ahead you know, that that was for me.
Yeah. He can really grab you. Bix is a little more subtle.
